auth.notes: Owner account and raw device record. No cloud endpoint, key or credential is reproduced. Replacement clients must use ordinary CA/hostname validation and currently supported TLS rather than copying the public Python client's disabled verification or legacy cipher choices.

cloud.failure_mode: Initial owner record acquisition and fresh provisioning stop without the service. Once bluetoothKey/deviceBindUserId are cached, local BLE session negotiation and read-only queries need no cloud. There is no supported redacted offline export/import workflow, and reset does not guarantee a new independent client can be provisioned offline.
cloud.notes: Official Wi-Fi onboarding requirements do not make later BLE traffic cloud-dependent. Raw TCP 4067 and Alink/CoAP are separate unevaluated channels.
cloud.vendor_service: FC SmartHome account/device service for initial bluetoothKey and deviceBindUserId

companion_apps.notes: Cloud device record supplies the initial bluetoothKey and deviceBindUserId. Later BLE sessions can be local.

identity.display: manual FC model selection followed by handshake model text
identity.notes: The BLE address and handshake MAC text are locators/identifiers, not proof of ownership or a substitute for deviceBindUserId; redact them in exports.

discovery.none: Manual exact-model selection. Scan service 000001fa and the name hints only reduce the list a user inspects; they never activate commands. Require the configured 0000ffe0/0000ffe1 endpoints or a validated notifiable alternative, then perform VERIFY_IDENTITY as the first write.

identification.notes: No safe automatic model matcher is declared. Name evidence includes Smart Lock, FC, Yi, EL, DX, K3, DZ, SL and L5; these are candidates only. Advertised scan service 000001fa-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and main service 0000ffe0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb are not unique proof of an L5 or of credential compatibility. Manual selection is mandatory.

device.name: FC SmartHome / Fingerchip BLE Locks
device.notes:
FC/Fingercrystal locks support local BLE after owner provisioning. The initial 16-byte bluetoothKey and 32-byte deviceBindUserId come from the owner's cloud device record. VERIFY_IDENTITY returns a per-session AES key used after the handshake. No general offline method for issuing the initial key or bind identity was found, and a MAC address is not a substitute.
The reliable initial surface is read-only: identity handshake, model, firmware, wake source, users and history. Device-information opcode 0x03 versus 0x04 and battery item types are unresolved, so no battery entity or information query is exposed. USER/0x04 command 0x10 data 0x01 is documented only as advanced attended unlock; the conflicting stale target form SYSTEM/0x02 command 0x0E must not be sent. Latch/beep and a generic lock action are not implemented by the active FC BLE client.
Consumer integration is identify_only: a custom encrypted/session handler is required. There are no generic commands or entities. Advertised names and the 0x01FA/FFE0 services are candidate filters, not model identity. Manual selection and a successful identity handshake are required before any later operation. No wake-prime heartbeat precedes that handshake.

openness.notes: Only one independent end-to-end FC implementation was found. This is not TTLock and no Tuya/TTLock provisioning or protocol compatibility is inferred.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: Official account/admin provisioning is required; there is no demonstrated unauthenticated local bind or pairing window for a replacement client.

procedures.basis: Official FC app manual and the public client's provisioning boundary; not run here.
procedures.name: Official FC account and administrator setup

steps.action: Use the official app's QR/back-panel or nearby/manual addition flow and complete administrator setup.
steps.expect: The owner device record contains the bluetoothKey and deviceBindUserId required by the first independent BLE session.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the other central, wake the lock and start a fresh connection; do not factory reset to resolve a busy link.

pairing.notes: Application-layer identity/key verification replaces an established OS BLE bond. Link-layer bonding behavior is not asserted.

unpair.clears: Official factory settings clears device credentials/history; no targeted local unpair operation is established.
unpair.notes: Do not treat OS Bluetooth forget, another lock ecosystem or an unused bind constant as a working unpair/bind route.

safety_advisory.detail: Complete identity verification and read-only checks first, wake the lock without repeatedly polling it, and keep a person at the door with an independent entry method. Send one intentional unlock only while awake and require its result/event. Never automate, replay after timeout or use discovery as authorization. User enrollment, fingerprint/card/password management and BLE factory reset are outside this spec.
safety_advisory.summary: The only supported actuation is advanced attended USER/0x04 command 0x10. Never send the stale SYSTEM/0x02 command 0x0E form or a generic unlock.

issued_to_client: Initial bluetoothKey: 32 hex characters decoded to 16 bytes
deviceBindUserId: 32 ASCII bytes, truncated/padded with NUL on the wire
Per-session AES key: 16 raw bytes returned by the handshake and never logged
credentials.notes: Wi-Fi provisioning protection is not established by the BLE research; no Wi-Fi credential is sent by this spec. Initial and session keys are owner secrets. The public cloud client can export raw sensitive records after login but offers no redacted offline importer; ordinary Android backup is disabled in FC SmartHome 4.6.6.
stored_on_device: Initial bluetoothKey and expected deviceBindUserId, with model-specific rotation behavior unknown
Per-session AES keys negotiated during VERIFY_IDENTITY
Users, access credentials and history, outside this spec's management scope

factory_reset.description: Use the official app's destructive factory-settings route for the exact model. The reviewed manual depicts E202Pro, not the community-tested L5, so it supports the app-flow consequence rather than a universal button or BLE reset command. No BLE reset command is recovered or recommended.
factory_reset.effect: The official app manual says factory settings delete the device and clear passwords, fingerprints, cards and message history. Treat local initial/session credentials and cached owner access as invalid; re-provision through the account. Reset is not an offline recovery path.

procedures.basis: FC SmartHome app manual for the depicted E202Pro; not executed and not generalized to L5.
procedures.name: Official app factory settings (model-specific)

steps.action: Keep the door attended, preserve any still-valid owner record if appropriate, and confirm the exact model in the official app.
Choose the official factory-settings action and confirm deletion of device credentials/history as the manual describes.
steps.expect: Passwords, fingerprints, cards and message history are cleared; complete account/admin provisioning again. Do not expect old BLE credentials to work.

cloud.local_alternative: No verified offline first-time issuance of bluetoothKey/deviceBindUserId. Once both are cached, later session keys are negotiated locally.

methods.description: Use official account setup and an owner-authorized private export of bluetoothKey and deviceBindUserId, then perform local BLE handshakes. There is no dedicated redacted offline export/importer in the public client, and Android backup is disabled in the reviewed release.
methods.name: Cloud device record once, then local session keys

steps.action: Complete official FC SmartHome account/admin setup; for a Wi-Fi model use its required 2.4 GHz network and preserve the owner device record privately.
Store bluetoothKey (32 hex chars) and deviceBindUserId (32 ASCII bytes) in a secret store; do not print, derive from a MAC, or substitute zeros/deviceuuid.
Manually select the lock, wake it with 4 then # for an approximately 60-second window when needed, subscribe to notifications and retry service discovery if the sleeping GATT table is partial.
Send VERIFY_IDENTITY at sequence 1 with the bind identity and current local time, accept only result 0 or 0xF1, and switch to the returned 16-byte session key.
steps.expect: Read-only model, firmware, protocol and wake-source fields validate before user/history queries. No heartbeat or actuation precedes this step.

causes: The lock is asleep. Wake it and retry discovery; require a notifiable characteristic before sending anything.
troubleshooting.symptom: The GATT table is empty or FFE1 is missing.

causes: Use the actual 32-byte deviceBindUserId, not zeros or the older deviceuuid label. Retry on a fresh connection with sequence 1 rather than advancing as if it succeeded.
Check whether the record's bluetoothKey differs from the public client's one-device fallback; do not assume every model shares that fallback.
troubleshooting.symptom: The identity attempt is ignored or rejected.

causes: The lock sleeps. Use 4 then # for the longer window and complete one read-only transaction at a time; do not repeatedly wake for polling.
troubleshooting.symptom: Commands time out after a short idle period.

setup.notes: Official setup uses an account and, for Wi-Fi models, a 2.4 GHz network. The owner's device record supplies bluetoothKey as 32 hex characters and deviceBindUserId as a 32-byte identity. Current research corrects older comments that called the latter deviceuuid. The active integration also has a built-in initial-key fallback that matched one tested L5, but that is one observation, not general offline issuance; deviceBindUserId still has no verified offline source. Do not rely on the fallback by default.

rejoin.notes: A cached bluetoothKey/deviceBindUserId can negotiate a fresh session without cloud contact while accepted. Rebinding a new independent client still needs an owner-authorized device record. Reset is not a routine recovery step and its credential-rotation behavior is unknown.

steps.action: Wake the lock and connect with the cached owner record on a fresh BLE connection.
Start at sequence 1, verify identity and require read-only model/firmware data before any further operation.

testing.notes: No lock, account, owner record, real key or live operation was used by this project. Protocol facts and the author's L5 live results are reported by the pinned public implementation; all vectors below are newly generated with invented keys/identities. A fixed public app-bundle frame corroborates only outer v2 framing/checksum and is not an over-the-air capture or a hardware run by this project.

variants.notes: The public author's live handshake/read/unlock evidence is L5-class. Other model names are discovery hints only, not protocol proof.
Depicted in the official app manual for account/factory-reset flow, not used to assert L5 protocol or credentials.

evidence.documentation_review: The official app manual supplies account/admin flow, 4+# wake and the destructive factory-settings consequence for the depicted E202Pro. The 2026-11-11 research supplement supplies the cloud-export, fallback, backup, TLS and no-public-firmware boundaries. No TTLock evidence exists.
evidence.open_questions: Owner-hardware read-only captures should establish dialect, response sequencing, model-specific records, info/battery opcodes and reset effects before any advanced unlock is considered. Raw TCP/CoAP and firmware remain outside the proven local BLE surface.
evidence.public_capture_boundary: A fixed public app-bundle frame independently corroborates outer FD/FE, little-endian total length and XOR checksum. It is not treated as an over-the-air capture, and no public fallback/initial key, real identity, session key, MAC or owner history is copied into this spec or its vectors.
evidence.public_implementation: JuanmanDev/fc-smart-home-assistant at e2f66d547e40fd4cfb9544f52bbc8eb98a5ac21c supplied v1/v2 framing, AES, handshake, sequencing, wake behavior, users/history and advanced unlock. Its offline protocol tests passed in the research packet; its author's L5 live results are third-party reported evidence, not this project's run.

initialization.notes: Require notifications and reassemble by outer little-endian total length, not ATT notification boundaries. Retry service discovery on a freshly woken lock if the table is partial.

initialization.description: Custom first write: VERIFY_IDENTITY at sequence 1 using the owner record. Accept only result 0/0xF1, install the returned session key, then validate read-only model/firmware/wake data. No generic client can execute this dynamic step.

v1 FC and v2 FD frame construction, zero-fill, XOR and fragmented reassembly
Users and history with pagination and unresolved semantics preserved
Documentary advanced attended USER/0x04 command 0x10 unlock
not_covered: Offline initial credential issuance or a MAC-only provisioning route
Generic unlock/lock/latch/beep, unattended actuation, stale SYSTEM/0x02 command 0x0E

local_access.summary: Local encrypted BLE after owner-record provisioning. identify_only in this catalogue until a dedicated strict session handler exists; read-only operations come first.

advanced_unlock_documentary.requirements: Only after successful identity and read-only checks, while awake, with a person attending the door. Send once and validate result/event; never auto-replay.
advanced_unlock_documentary.result_handling: Only result 0 confirms the documentary unlock. Result 0xF1 is accepted solely for VERIFY_IDENTITY, not for unlock. Every other result, including 0xF1, is unconfirmed/failure and must not be replayed.

stale_target_correction.action: DO NOT SEND. The active source/protocol tests support 0x04/0x10, not this conflicting target-stub form.

advanced_unlock_documentary.status: not a generic command and not offered by this catalogue entry

advanced_unlock_documentary.unsupported: Latch, beep, generic lock alias, unattended automation, enrollment, fingerprint/card/password management and factory reset.
advanced_unlock_documentary.user_credited_variant: USER/0x04 command 0x18 with uint16 LE user id exists in the public client but is outside the minimal safe scope and is not offered.

consumer_limitations.required_handler: Manual selection + wake/GATT negotiation + initial/session AES + strict FC/FD reassembly + identity/session sequencing + read-only-first safety gate.

session_sequencing.after_response: Next request sequence = response.sequence + 1 modulo 2^32, not simply local_previous + 1. Full uint32 is retained.
session_sequencing.failed_handshake: Reconnect and send sequence 1 again; do not advance as if the failed handshake succeeded.
session_sequencing.first: Sequence 1 on each fresh connection, always for the identity handshake.
session_sequencing.retransmission: Read-only retries resend the identical frame/sequence. An unlock is never automatically retried after timeout.

inner_message.v1: No trailing inner XOR; inner_length = 8 + data length.
inner_message.v2: One trailing inner XOR; inner_length = 9 + data length including that XOR.
inner_message.v2_xor_android_heartbeat: The special Android heartbeat additionally XORs all four little-endian sequence bytes. Do not apply this variant to every message.
inner_message.v2_xor_normal: length_low XOR length_high XOR category XOR command XOR every data byte
inner_message.validation: Require minimum inner lengths (8/9), exact inner length within decrypted data, valid v2 XOR, and all zero-fill bytes after inner_length.

out_of_scope_transports.alink_coap_udp_5683: Gateway/LAN registration and CoAP are documented by the public client but not evaluated in this packet; no local actuation is claimed.
out_of_scope_transports.raw_tcp_4067: Reported cloud socket/NAT-DNS redirect not evaluated end-to-end; do not present it as a working local unlock path or reuse the BLE framing there.

crypto.length_rule: Use the inner length to find real data and require every zero-fill byte after it to be zero; padding alone is not a length delimiter.
crypto.padding: Append zero bytes only to the next 16-byte boundary. An already aligned inner message gets no extra block.
crypto.session_key: 16 raw bytes returned by VERIFY_IDENTITY; use for every subsequent message and never log

outer_frame.implementation_bound: The public parser uses a 1024-byte frame ceiling as a defensive input bound; do not allocate unbounded buffers for hostile lengths.

layout.description: Package index; users/history pagination continues until response pid is zero
layout.name: pid

layout.formula: pid XOR length_low XOR length_high XOR every encrypted byte
layout.name: outer_checksum

outer_frame.reassembly: Scan to FC/FD, wait for total_length, require total length >=22, ciphertext multiple of 16, FE terminator and valid outer checksum before decrypting. Drop malformed/corrupt frames and rescan; one ATT notification is not necessarily one frame.

device_information.conflict: Active HA method uses SYSTEM command 0x03; older protocol library labels READ_INFO 0x04. No captured proof resolves the difference.
device_information.guidance: Do not issue either opcode in the minimal subset and do not expose a battery sensor. Handshake already supplies model/firmware/wake.
device_information.response_items: Three-byte type,value-low,value-high. Types 18/19 display second.third; other types are uint16 LE. Item/battery meanings still need a real response.

history.privacy: User types, attributes, timestamps and record semantics are not asserted. Redact user identities/history in exported research.
history.record_size_heuristic: Choose 9 bytes when remaining length is divisible by 9 and at most 54, otherwise 8. This is a client heuristic, not a universal model guarantee; reject leftover partial records.
history.response: First data byte must be zero/status; following bytes are unlock/alarm records. Continue while response pid is nonzero and retain raw history privately.

users.malformed: Reject trailing partial records and nonzero status; do not silently floor a malformed payload into plausible users.

record.name: enabled
record.values: 1 means enabled; preserve other raw values

users.response: First data byte must be zero/status; following bytes are 22-byte records. Continue with response pid until zero.

transport.discovery_retry: A sleeping lock can expose an empty/partial GATT table. Retry service discovery, require a notifiable characteristic, and use configured FFE0/FFE1 or a validated compatible alternative.

wake.long_window: Press 4 then # on the keypad for approximately 60 seconds of BLE/Wi-Fi activity (reported on L5).
wake.polling: Do not repeatedly wake for polling. Complete advanced operations only while awake and attended.
wake.short_window: Keypad touch/bell or normal fingerprint/handle use wakes for a few seconds.

fields.description: Owner cloud-record identity, not zeros and not the stale deviceuuid label
fields.name: deviceBindUserId

fields.description: Signed hours in client convention, positive for UTC+N; negative values use two's complement
fields.name: timezone_hours

response.key_handling: Install response bytes 1..16 as the new session key only after accepting the result and validating the complete response; do not log it or the MAC/identity.
response.malformed: Reject short responses, non-accepted result, bad text encoding or truncated required fields rather than switching keys or publishing model data.

remaining_unknowns: Offline issuance/recovery of deviceBindUserId and initial bluetoothKey on other models; one L5 fallback match is not a general answer.
Model/firmware matrix for v1 versus v2, initial-key uniqueness and credential rotation after reset.
Device-information command 0x03 versus 0x04 and battery/item-type semantics; no battery reading is exposed.
History/user timestamp epoch/unit, user types/attributes, record-size heuristic across models and wake-source enum.
Safe characteristic fallback identity and bonding/central limits across models.
Raw TCP 4067 redirect, Alink/CoAP, Android effective trust/pinning, firmware artifacts/update behavior and Tuya/TTLock cross-compatibility (not claimed).

characteristics.name: FC encrypted write and notify
characteristics.notes: Whole FC/FD frames are split into <=20-byte writes without response, paced about 20 ms. No plaintext commands are declared.

services.name: FC encrypted BLE service
services.notes: Main service; advertised scan filter 000001fa-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb is separate. Neither is automatic model identity. Some sleeping units expose a partial table, and a dedicated client may learn a compatible notifiable alternative rather than assuming FFE1 exists.
